title: Wide, hybrid or narrow tables?

rows.label: In one line
values: One row per entity and moment, one column per metric
A metric-name column plus one value column per data type
One row per entity, moment and metric

rows.label: Shape
values: `(time, host, cpu, mem, disk)`
`(time, host, metric, value_float, value_int, value_text)`
`(time, host, metric, value)`

rows.label: Adding a metric
values: `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`, and every query and ingest job that lists columns
Insert rows with the new name; only a new data type adds a column
Insert rows with the new name

rows.label: Rows for one reading of six metrics
Value types
values: Each metric has its own native type
Native types, but something must map each metric to its column
One type (often a double); otherwise a table per type, or JSONB and casts

rows.label: Reading many metrics together
values: One row, no joins
Filter on `metric`, pivot, and `CASE` across types
A pivot, or a join per metric

rows.label: Sparse data
values: NULL cells when values arrive apart; cheap in columnar storage
NULLs in the unused type columns
No NULLs: a missing value is a missing row

rows.label: Compression (TigerData’s rating)
values: Good: NULL-heavy columns compress well
Good: uniform typed columns
Excellent: uniform columns

rows.label: Reach for it when
values: Metrics are known, stable and read together
Metrics come and go but fall into a few types, or differ per tenant
Metrics come and go and are read one series at a time

rows.label: Where you see it
values: Host and sensor tables; InfluxDB points with several fields; ArcticDB frames with very many columns
TigerData’s medium layout; fixed columns plus `jsonb` or a ClickHouse `Map`
Prometheus series; OpenTelemetry metrics in ClickHouse; pandas `melt()` output

tip: Start from how you read, not how data arrives. If dashboards show many metrics of one thing at one moment and the list is stable, go wide. If metrics come and go and are read one series at a time, go narrow. If they come and go but you want native types, add typed value columns. Mixing is normal: TigerData suggests a wide table for core metrics and a medium table for custom ones. Moving between layouts later means rewriting history, so when unsure, pick the one that extends without migrations.
